candidate.title: 5'-GRO-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina single-route schematic of 5′-GRO-Seq: Br-UTP nuclear run-on, RNA fragmentation and 3′ end repair, bromouridine-fragment immunocapture, uncapped-end dephosphorylation, cap removal, differential adapter acquisition and cDNA generation/amplification. The card title and verified RNA-collection page 34 identify the same target. GRO-Seq is the run-on context, not another target workflow. The two retained RNA drawings depict capped versus uncapped chemical classes within one pool; they are not alternative methods. Primary-paper details clarify the depicted implementation rather than expanding to unshown library-preparation variants.

states.label: Nuclear transcription complexes bearing nascent RNA
features: The target is nascent RNA with an intact 5′ 7-methylguanylated (m7G) cap, shown emerging from a chromatin-associated transcription complex.
The card supplies the nuclear-material context. This is an input/target illustration, not a separate detection reaction.

features: Br-UTP-derived bromouridine is incorporated into nascent RNA during run-on; orange stars mark the incorporation, rather than a barcode or a cap.
The original 5′ region is retained in the elongated RNA; the following fragment panel includes both capped and uncapped molecules and an unstarred background fragment.

features: The upper, formerly capped species has lost its cap; its 3′ OH and BrU mark remain.
The lower, already uncapped species retains its 5′ OH and 3′ OH.

The drawing leaves the newly decapped 5′ end chemically unlabeled. TAP is the paper-supported decapping enzyme; selective 5′-adapter acquisition in the next panel identifies the formerly capped end as ligation competent.

This is one product class within the common ligation mixture, not a separately depicted isolation.

features: The lower ligation product retains a left-hand 5′ OH and gains only the orange right-hand 3′ adapter.
This nonproductive class for two-adapter amplification remains explicitly depicted in the same mixture; no separate discard operation is shown.

evidence.locator: Ligate adaptors with truncated mutant RNA ligase 2 and RNA ligase 1; upper RNA has pink left and orange right adapter, lower RNA only orange right adapter
Reverse transcription amplification; common rightward arrow from adapter-ligated RNA to blue line labeled cDNA
evidence.rationale: The shared block amplifies adapter-bearing cDNA products. A species lacking the depicted 5′ adapter lacks that adapter-derived amplification interface; this is a library-competence interpretation, not a claim of perfect experimental removal.

states.label: Amplified cDNA library representing captured nascent capped 5′ RNA ends
features: The terminal blue line is explicitly labeled cDNA; RNA sequence information is carried into a DNA library by reverse transcription and amplification.
The intended productive insert derives from a fragment retaining both its original capped 5′ boundary and incorporated BrU through selection, then receiving both adapters.

The supported readout maps nascent 5′ ends and transcription start-site activity, including enhancer RNA initiation. It does not by itself establish full transcript structures or steady-state abundance.

Representation requires BrU incorporation and retention of a cap-bearing, BrU-positive fragment through preparation. The schematic supplies no quantitative capture efficiency or claim of exhaustive biological specificity.
Sequencing is described by the card, but the assigned drawing ends at cDNA and does not show a separate sequencing or computational-analysis operation.

evidence.rationale: The productive two-adapter class supplies the library. Combining BrU capture with the cap-dependent adapter pattern explains the intended nascent capped-end readout; selection and conversion efficiency are not specified as perfect.

evidence.rationale: Hydrolysis breaks transcript connectivity, while the productive species must satisfy both BrU capture and cap-dependent 5′-adapter acquisition. The library therefore samples selected nascent capped fragments rather than intact transcript structures or every RNA molecule present.

operations.label: Run-on with analog
operations.description: Extend nascent RNA in nuclear material using the depicted Br-UTP analog, producing RNA with incorporated BrU marks while retaining the pre-existing 5′ region.
operations.mechanism: Br-UTP is an incorporation substrate. The card reports sarkosyl during nuclear run-on to inhibit additional RNAPII binding; no additional nuclear preparation stages are drawn.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a physical bromouridine label linking recoverable RNA to run-on synthesis by engaged transcription complexes.

operations.label: DNase treatment and hydrolyze
operations.description: Remove DNA from the run-on material and hydrolyze RNA into shorter fragments. The resulting population includes capped labeled, uncapped labeled and unlabeled fragments.
operations.mechanism: DNase treatment acts on contaminating DNA; hydrolysis fragments the RNA. These are retained as the single combined preparation block shown by the source caption.
operations.information_effect: Fragmentation breaks whole-transcript continuity. A cap-bearing fragment must itself retain BrU to survive the subsequent label selection.

evidence.rationale: Antibody capture acts on BrU-bearing fragments after hydrolysis, so a fragment that retains a cap but no BrU is not selected by that criterion.

operations.label: 3′ dephosphorylate with polynucleotide kinase
operations.description: Convert the fragmented RNA 3′ ends to hydroxyl ends; all three depicted fragment classes are carried forward with right-hand OH labels.
operations.mechanism: The named polynucleotide kinase is used here for its 3′-dephosphorylation function; it is an enzyme, not a transferred library component.
operations.information_effect: Makes the RNA 3′ end compatible with the later 3′-adapter interface while preserving cap status and BrU identity.

operations.label: Bead coated with α-BrUTP antibody
operations.description: Capture bromouridine-bearing RNA fragments on antibody-coated beads. The selected fraction includes capped and uncapped labeled RNA; the unlabeled fragment is omitted from the downstream depiction.
operations.mechanism: The diagram bead caption says α-BrUTP antibody. The primary 5′-GRO-Seq methods identify anti-BrdU agarose beads used to precipitate labeled RNA fragments; the architecture therefore uses RNA-fragment immunocapture, not free-nucleotide selection.
operations.information_effect: Enriches the run-on-labeled fragment population without selecting caps. Disappearance of the unstarred icon expresses intended enrichment rather than measured perfect specificity.

operations.label: Cap removal
operations.description: Remove the cap from the upper selected RNA, generating the end that receives the 5′ adapter later. The uncapped 5′ OH class remains unchanged.

operations.label: Ligate adaptors with truncated mutant RNA ligase 2 and RNA ligase 1
operations.description: Add the orange 3′ adapter to both RNA classes and the pink 5′ adapter only to the formerly capped class. The two outputs are chemical classes in a common reaction pool, not a physical split into separate libraries.

operations.information_effect: The two-adapter class carries the original capped 5′ end at an adapter junction and acquires both library interfaces; the uncapped class is depicted with only one interface.

operations.description: Process the common ligation mixture through the broad reverse-transcription/amplification block to obtain cDNA. RNA provides the insert sequence; amplification yields library molecules with both adapter interfaces.

method_scopes.rationale: All eight local transformations belong to the single 5′-GRO-Seq route. The far-left Detect nascent RNA caption identifies the biological target rather than adding an assay step. The primary paper explicitly describes 5′-GRO-Seq with the depicted order and identifies the decapping enzyme and ligase assignments. Its conventional GRO-Seq library protocol is a different section and is not substituted into this schematic. The cap-dependent two-adapter class and uncapped 3′-only class are both retained as outputs of the common ligation block. The implementation uses cap state and BrU labeling jointly; it does not establish identical behavior for all capped-RNA or GRO-family assays.
